BERT4Rec averages masked-target losses within each sequence and uses appended-mask inference; its original design also includes terminal-only training examples. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690). A controlled ablation should compare terminal-only T, reconstruction-only R, and L=0.5T+0.5R, where R first averages targets per sequence, then averages sequences. This gives objectives equal coefficients, not equal gradient magnitudes. Explicitly distinguish this simultaneous weighted loss from choosing one objective with probability 0.5: their expected gradients may agree, but gradient variance and Adam updates differ.

Recommended controls: clone identical seed-42 initialization per category; retain preprocessing seed 0, backbone, splits, optimizer settings, batch size, 200 batches/epoch and ≤200 epochs. Replay identical users, endpoints and windows using separate sampling/corruption RNG streams. Construct terminal inputs by replacing the sampled endpoint with the reserved mask, excluding subsequent interactions. Fix reconstruction mask rate, eligible positions, replacement policy and empty-mask handling; state whether endpoints participate. Reuse each objective’s corruption across its standalone and mixed arms. Preserve left padding and final-nonpadding readout. Match sequence exposure and optimizer-update counts; combine both losses before one mixed-arm update. Equal updates do not imply equal supervised-target counts or compute: record targets, tokens, forward/backward passes and GPU-seconds separately. Target-matched and compute-matched comparisons answer additional questions.

Predeclare identical validation cadence, checkpoint-selection rule and tie-breaking using macro HR@10 across all four categories; also report a common fixed-update endpoint. On a few fixed paired minibatches at initialization and matched training steps, measure T/R losses, gradient norms, cosine similarity and weighted contributions, controlling dropout without updating parameters or consuming training RNG. Negative cosine indicates local conflict, not demonstrated downstream harm; this diagnostic follows [gradient-interference analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782). These controls are proposed experimental design, not reported findings.
